problem: Existing semantic maps either are flat (ConceptGraphs, DualMap), offline hierarchical (HOV-SG), or rely on dense embedding similarity retrieval (Embodied-RAG), which is fragile under negation, chained spatial constraints and other compositional queries, and cannot be maintained on-the-fly.
motivation: Robots must follow complex human instructions with negation, ambiguity and chained spatial constraints, which requires a structured, semantically rich, incrementally maintained and interpretable map. Serializing the scene graph into text lets LLMs index and reason over it RAG-style rather than matching embeddings.
key_idea: Build a four-level (floor/room/area/object) scene graph incrementally with an asynchronous geometric/semantic dual stream and event-triggered updates, then retrieve targets via multi-role LLM constraint parsing, weighted polarity-aware scoring with GraphRAG spatial traversal, and SAM3+VLM visual verification.
insight: Explicit logical decomposition (negation flags, intent weights, spatial graph traversal) plus visual verification is what handles complex queries. In the ablation on one HM3DSem-SQR sequence, removing VLM verification gives the biggest drop (74.0 to 65.4 SR, latency halves), removing SAM3 gives 68.5, and removing area nodes gives 71.7. Local VLM deployment cuts query latency from 25.93 s to 10.42 s.
method: Hierarchical scene graph: floor/room/area/object nodes with interlayer (hierarchy) and intralayer (spatial topology) edges; nodes store VLM/LLM natural-language summaries, DINOv3 features and 3D centroids, serialized to graphs/tables for LLM retrieval.

Geometric stream: ~2 Hz BEV occupancy from depth raycasting, room segmentation via EDT + watershed with doors as boundaries and hysteresis voting, floor nodes from vertical motion; DINOv3 cosine-similarity keyframe gating pushes informative frames to a queue.

Semantic stream: asynchronous SAM3 instance masks, back-projected centroids, DINOv3 features, VLM descriptions for new nodes; area clustering per room with LLM functional labels; room description from best-view image plus area summaries.

Node association: two-stage fusion using 3D distance, DINOv3 similarity and SentenceTransformer text similarity, with different rules for predefined-label and open-vocabulary objects; weighted moving-average fusion; pairwise relations via geometric or VLM mode.

Event-triggered updates: hard trigger (floor change) and soft trigger (VLM supervisor examines a fading BEV map with rooms/trajectory/update points on room entry); then room mask optimization (pruning, line regularization, EDT competition) and bottom-up rebuild of area/room nodes.

Interpretable retrieval: multi-role LLM parses target/landmark/spatial constraints, negation flags and importance weights; score S(n)=H_floor·Σ p_i·w_i·Sim(n,c_i) with GraphRAG traversal of the spatial graph for relations.
Visual verification: SAM3 prompted with the target label on the candidate's best-view image (fall back to next candidate if nothing found), then a VLM validates the query; outputs the 3D centroid.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (cloud, frozen) for LLM/VLM; Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct as local alternative; SAM3, DINOv3, SentenceTransformer (frozen)
setting.observation: RGB-D stream with poses (real world: SLAM poses, Livox LiDAR-derived depth)
setting.action_space: none (retrieval of 3D target centroid; no navigation policy evaluated)
setting.privileged: none stated (human-teleoperated exploration trajectories used as input)

numbers_note: Ablation SRs (74.0 full, 71.7, 68.5, 65.4) are given in text on a single random HM3DSem-SQR sequence; the appendix table is not included, so they are not listed as entries.
results: INHerit-SG reaches 36.3% average accuracy within 1 m on HM3DSem-SQR versus 33.02 for the strongest baseline DualMap, and 28.9% at 0.5 m versus 28.01. In human evaluation it scores 79.7/72.9/70.6 (QLCR/AHAR/ALMA) versus 66.1/54.2/59.8 for ConceptGraphs, and 60.0% versus 35.0% on real-world queries. The scene graph is 34.0-47.5 MB versus 87.4 MB for DualMap and 18.47 GB for ConceptGraphs.
limitations: Cannot handle highly dynamic layouts or frequent object rearrangements, and lifelong operation is left to future work.
Absolute accuracies on HM3DSem-SQR are low (about 36% at 1 m), and the cloud VLM pipeline has high latency (about 22-26 s per query).
Evaluated only on retrieval of target locations, not closed-loop navigation; baseline comparison with human evaluation covers only some baselines.
